title: Thorn
imageAlt: Portrait of Thorn, a Veilguard and returned survivor
dek: A loud, practical goblin druid who puts out fires, bargains for cattle and keeps returning for her companions. Her work joins Pristinia’s rebuilding, Aionia’s rescue, the Veilguard and the groves she still hopes to grow.

body:
Thorn is a goblin druid who shouts orders through smoke, rides a giant toad and bargains as fiercely for work animals as she fights for companions. Her impatience can be exhausting. So can the tenderness she tries to disguise with a complaint or a joke.

Long before her death on Gael, she is already putting nature magic to work for Pristinia. Her call helps bring the Great Stag to Aionia, and Serath’s sacrifice leaves her grieving beside Modeli. Later, her own recovery returns her to the Veilguard, to fields and dangerous journeys, and to the hope of growing a grove on every island.

Reliability before honeyed words

At the leadership tests, Thorn measures a leader by whether the tribe stays fed, mostly alive and moving in the same direction. Honor means keeping an agreement and watching someone’s back; wisdom includes recognizing the too-quiet forest and surviving when a plan fails. Her humor is rough, but the concern beneath it is practical trust.

The imagined battlefield choice troubles her. She proposes a small rescue party while the rest hold the line, then chooses to pursue the relic that might end the war. She does not call the decision clean. When asked to assess possible leaders, she distrusts conclusions drawn from attractive speeches alone: conduct is what reveals a person. These are her positions during a test, not an account of a battle already fought.

Belonging to the Veilguard

Thorn says, “I belong with the Veilguard, so I must return.”

Ordinary institutional life

Thorn also carries news of Farkur and the Ale-Chemy Knights’ disappearance, Ryvyt’s response, Gael transport, farms, and harvest work. A person who passed through death and cult ritual still participates in the mundane systems by which regions continue.

27 March 2026 · leading into The Before

Thorn leads the joint Pristinian–Rahuvian survey once the scholars arrive. She identifies the briars’ Delerium scent, bottles some of the purple haze for later study, and helps move the group through the changed entrance. The work places her at the boundary between field instinct and formal scholarship.

29 May 2026 · tracking through Howl

Thorn helps free and heal a deer caught in a bear trap, searches around the winter cabin, and later finds the wolf tracks that lead toward the den. Her contribution is not a single finishing blow. It is the sequence that turns a frightened wilderness scene into a route the party can follow.

10 October · restraint at the embassy

Thorn arrives in Pristinia through a Gate she credits to Adelia and says she came to check the farm and greenhouses. She joins the graffiti investigation, acknowledges her hatred of the Rahu after the war and nevertheless promises to behave while the party approaches the embassy.

The Dasa’s request brings her wartime memories into contact with people asking for freedom from their own hierarchy. The party departs with a promised search, without a completed liberation. Read the appeal.

Scene sources: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Belonging does not remove danger

Thorn’s later account of returning to Gael connects preparation with belonging: she will equip herself because she belongs with the Veilguard. Her reassurance that its members watch out for one another describes mutual responsibility, rather than a guarantee that nobody will be lost.

The recovered aftermath now supplies a means of attempted restoration: Alyhotep begins a Wish-based resurrection after the party retrieves her body. Her later living presence is established; the exact spell-completion moment remains unrecorded in the checked excerpt.

Magic that helps a harvest

Her plans to bless farmland belong beside the field work already in this history. They show an intention to support food production with nature magic; the plan is not a recorded yield or proof that the spell was performed. Tracking, healing and cultivation can all contribute to keeping a place habitable.

A connector in Gael’s daily life

Thorn describes the Ale-Chemy market and explains that she helps acquire things without being a Knight herself. Her account of Farkur and others having vanished remains attributed language. It does not establish death, disbanding or the cause of absence.

She also describes a trusted route for transporting known people to Gael. The testimony supports a social connection, not universal safe passage or a promise that travel now has no cost. Gael’s earlier restorers and continuing defenders remain part of the same history; no generational ranking replaces their quest-established work.

Recorded scenes

Dates refer to transcript postings.

    7–8 September 2026 · brought home

    Thorn dies during a husk hunt in Gael. The team is forced to leave the body. A cult later attempts to use Thorn in a ritual aimed at one of Gael’s Shards. By 8 September 2026, Thorn is alive and recovering at the Tower of Gael; she later appears alive in Prima on 19 September.

    Recovery: the retrieved body, Ryvyt’s removal of the strange oil and Alyhotep’s Wish-based resurrection attempt now connect the stages. Thorn is subsequently alive; the precise spell-completion moment is not explicitly narrated in the recovered excerpt.

    Severina carries Thorn’s body back after the expedition finds it near Stake. The narrator describes it covered in strange oils and unguents. Ryvyt applies alchemical preparations; when they mix with what is already on the body, there is a brief flash and no oil remains. The party reaches the Tower of Gael.

    Severina asks Alyhotep whether he can bring Thorn back. He says he can use an arcane Wish to perform a normal resurrection and begins making that Wish without material components. This is a recorded attempt, beyond the earlier general hope of recovering her.

    By 8 September, Thorn is moving about the Tower and asks for warm tea in a low, scratchy voice. Alyhotep asks whether she needs more healing. These later scenes establish her living recovery. They do not supply a separate narrator description of the precise moment the Wish completes.

    September · returning does not mean being well

    The Tower conversation continues after Thorn first appears alive. She asks for tea in a scratchy voice, describes feeling dreadful and tells the others she died. Farkur greets her with relief and later offers somewhere she can rest, saying there is no shame in needing it.

    This strengthens the record of her living recovery and its physical aftermath. It does not supply the missing narrator description of Alyhotep’s spell completing, and her weakness is not turned into a universal rule about every resurrection. Returning to the community includes being allowed time to recover.

    Aerial warning and a proposal to grow food

    Thorn identifies a hallucinogenic trace on the attacked workers’ clothing, while its ingredients and delivery remain unknown. On the road she flies above the carts as an eagle and warns of approaching horses before the attackers arrive.

    After the fight she talks with the archers, offers to teach cultivation and proposes magic to improve a harvest. These are offers of another source of food; no new farm or completed harvest is shown. The raiders’ later agreement is only a pause while a meeting is arranged.

    Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

    A grove imagined, a companion brought back

    At the observatory, Thorn speaks of wanting groves on the islands and is frustrated by people she sees as selfish. Clive’s fear that being odd makes him disposable gets a kinder answer: there is nothing wrong with being odd. Her judgments of the town’s supply problems remain judgments, based in part on a sign she reports seeing.

    Later she and Pell approach a sea serpent from the Remote Fishing Village on Toadimus. She wants to talk to or tame it and prepares ways to get Pell out if the attempt becomes dangerous. They withdraw before a fight is established. Thorn takes wing and carries him away; a sudden storm obscures the village, and she flies them toward the Twilight Observatory. No captured serpent or new guardian of the shipping lanes results.

    A grove is a goal she still has to explain

    Thorn tells her companions on the coast that she wants to make a grove on every discovered island. Reuniting the separated lands is another hope, and she admits she has not thought through every part of it. She wants help with ideas she knows may need correcting.

    Scribonia warns that wanting a result without firmer limits may leave her open to an enemy offering it. Kasiri challenges the way he gives that warning, while Severina speaks in support of what Thorn has done. Thorn’s ambitions remain hers: no completed network of groves, joined islands or uncontested lesson follows from this conversation.

    A fire needs water before a speech

    During the siege of Pristinia, Thorn arrives coughing and immediately demands that someone do something about the fires. She looks for water, then calls on the taller adventurers and Camilla to gather it. Her magic has limits; she needs them to help make the one useful casting count.

    With Navi’s help, she gathers a great sphere of water and bursts it over the flames. The narrator describes cleared smoke and a better chance of finding shelter. The effort does not put the whole city beyond danger: Thorn is herself caught in the fire that follows.

    Underground, she makes little ice toads dance for the children because their crying is giving her a headache. The children laugh. She examines a mother’s burns, offers poultices and names her price as a raspberry tart sometime in the future. When danger approaches, she reaches for her pot-lid shield and moves to protect the children. Her complaints stay loud while her hands keep finding work.

    What a saved animal could help build

    On the later Eovar supply trip, Thorn hears cattle calling from their cages. She asks whether, if she gets them free, they will help Pristinia by pulling wagons, plows and the frames of buildings. Their fear of being eaten meets her immediate idea of what the town needs.

    Fulmin insists that she purchase them rather than create another dispute with the locals. Thorn turns to bargaining. She asks the cattle for something embarrassing about the merchant, uses what she hears to press the price down and pays the agreed amount. The merchant finally agrees to sell her a cow, and she pays the accepted price.

    That does not finish the farm she imagines. She still needs somewhere to keep the animal, land to plow and materials. She buys supplies and offers to pull the carts herself by changing shape. Cultivation is already a practical interest in these early quests, well before her later promises to bless a harvest or grow groves.

    Calling until something answers

    In the First Forest, Thorn’s trust in nature has to survive magic that no longer behaves. An intended spell leaves her sick; another forces her to attack Arethusa. She is shaken afterward. When she recognizes the danger of more casting, Aionia praises her restraint and asks her to call the Great Stag.

    Thorn changes form and keeps calling through the sickness. She offers a way to carry the wounded goddess as the violet mist approaches. After Aionia falls, she begs nature to let the Stag hear. The narrator finally shows it on the horizon.

    She also offers her own life alongside Serath and urges Modeli to help. The attempt does not take her soul. Serath’s does enter Aionia, and the Great Stag later lends its strength. Aionia thanks Thorn for answering the request and promises that the land will know bounty; that promise is not a recorded harvest.

    Thorn stays beside the body long enough to pray through tears. The friend who could make children laugh with water cannot make this loss harmless. Read Serath’s sacrifice →

    A companion whose coat she can cut

    On the road from Emberwillow toward Larkhollow, Thorn climbs onto Modeli’s back. She keeps slipping; he gives her his knife and tells her to cut handholds and footholds in his coat. She does. Their cooperation has room for an uncomfortable knee, an aching back and the practical advantage of keeping the small druid where she can see.

    They arrange watches and exchange ideas about the creatures ahead. She offers to make him a dinosaur if a fight comes; he would rather remain himself and help from the rear. When she falls, he reaches for her. When danger arrives, he encourages her to change form as she had planned.

    These are the same two people who offered themselves beside Serath. Their later company still includes embarrassment, teasing and looking out for one another. It is an ordinary relationship that the sacrifice did not end.

    The grove she wants and the work in front of her

    The later Dark Shroud expedition gives Thorn an immediate task beside the groves she hopes to grow. She and Trougar travel with Minerva through an argument-filled search until they reach Yen fighting around an inscribed stone.

    Thorn takes an earth elemental’s form and joins the defence. Covering the attacks gives Minerva time to read. The company gains an inscription and a later mirror vision, but neither settles why the First Passage changed. Yen still has to fight when they leave.

    Thorn’s wish for a grove on every island therefore remains a wish with work and questions attached. On this journey, helping means holding the next attack while someone else tries to learn what went wrong. Read the Dark Shroud expedition →

profile.personality: Thorn is a field leader who treats belonging as an obligation: she regards the Veilguard as a community she must return to. She combines instinctive caution with practical curiosity, gathering evidence without pretending that every contaminated sign already has an explanation.
profile.achievements: A Veilguard member whose work in healing, field investigation and rebuilding continues alongside an unresolved history of death and return. Identifies a hallucinogenic trace and warns the caravan of mounted attackers before offering food-growing help.
profile.relationships: The Veilguard anchors Thorn’s sense of self. Lady Severina, Miri, and the Rahuvian scholars share her survey work, while Minerva and Jéane Rose help transform the Howl clues into action. Thorn also carries news of Farkur’s disappearance and Ryvyt’s grief, showing that a returned survivor still participates in the ordinary work of remembering other people’s losses.
